skill.name: Curve segment lifecycle management
skill.description: Manage the lifecycle of line and area segments by starting, adding points, and ending segments in the correct sequence. This micro-skill ensures proper demarcation of segment boundaries and point rendering within each segment.
skill.skill_body:
Execute the segment lifecycle in strict order: (1) call lineStart() or areaStart() to begin a new segment, (2) call point(x, y) one or more times to add vertices, (3) call lineEnd() or areaEnd() to close the segment. Do not interleave segment types or call end before start.

## Objective

Execute point-to-segment rendering sequence
## Applicable Signals

- Rendering a line or area shape
- Need to demarcate segment boundaries
- Adding points within each segment
- Constructing continuous shapes from discrete points

## Contraindications

- Rendering single isolated points without segment structure
- Working with pre-rendered paths that do not require segment demarcation
- No segment structure required for the output
- Calling point() before calling lineStart() or areaStart()
- Calling lineEnd() or areaEnd() without a corresponding start call

## Intervention Moves

- Call lineStart() to begin a line segment
- Call areaStart() to begin an area segment
- Call point(x, y) to add a vertex to the current segment
- Call lineEnd() to close the current line segment
- Call areaEnd() to close the current area segment

## Workflow Steps

- Call lineStart() or areaStart() to begin a new segment
- Call point(x, y) one or more times to add vertices
- Call lineEnd() or areaEnd() to close the segment

## Constraints

- lineStart/areaStart must be called before any point() calls
- point() calls must occur between start and end calls
- lineEnd/areaEnd must be called to close each segment
- Do not interleave line and area segment types within the same sequence
- Segment boundaries must be properly closed before starting a new segment

## Cautions

- Forgetting to call the corresponding end method will leave the segment open and may cause rendering errors
- Calling point() outside of a segment context (before start or after end) will fail silently or produce undefined behavior
- Mixing lineStart/lineEnd with areaStart/areaEnd in the same sequence may produce unexpected output

## Output Contract

- Completed line or area segment with all points rendered and segment boundaries properly closed. The segment is ready for downstream rendering or further transformation.

## Example Executions

### Example 1

- Input: Line segment with three points: (0, 0), (10, 5), (20, 0)
- Output: lineStart() → point(0, 0) → point(10, 5) → point(20, 0) → lineEnd()
- Notes: Produces a polyline connecting the three points.

### Example 2

- Input: Area segment with four points: (0, 0), (10, 10), (20, 10), (30, 0)
- Output: areaStart() → point(0, 0) → point(10, 10) → point(20, 10) → point(30, 0) → areaEnd()
- Notes: Produces a filled area bounded by the four vertices.
